transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this round-robin review regarding the fourteen 55-gallon drums of spent coolant currently staged in the waste staging area. The disposal vendor hasn't received authorization yet, so I need to walk through the removal plan with laboratory quality, waste logistics, and warehouse supervision before I can approve the disposal route and shipment controls. Let's get started — does anyone have initial observations or concerns about the current state of the drums or the proposed disposal approach?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. I need to share an important finding from my laboratory analysis completed yesterday. The spent coolant was found to contain 2.4% chlorinated solvent, which exceeds our site waste matrix threshold of 1.0%. At or above that level, the batch must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. This result has not yet been attached to the waste authorization, but it's critical for determining the correct disposal route for these fourteen drums.

transcript.text: Elena, before we finalize the shipment controls, I need to flag a permit constraint I confirmed with the disposal contractor. Their tanker permit allows no more than 8 of these drums on a single load, so the 14 drums will need to be shipped as two separate loads — one load of 8 and a second load of 6. I received this condition in the contractor's service email but have not yet entered it into the transport booking system, so we need to account for this in the removal plan.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to report a critical finding from my warehouse inspection. I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 drums. Those 4 drums must each be placed in a UN-rated overpack before any movement, while the other 10 can remain on their existing spill pallets. I recorded this on the shift clipboard, but I want to make sure everyone here is aware — the waste file has not been updated yet, so this needs to be factored into the removal plan and shipment controls.
